description.text: This resolution recognizes and thanks Mae Krier on her 100 th birthday for her contributions to the United States as a trailblazer and a Rosie the Riveter (a term used to describe women who joined the workforce during World War II).

latestAction.text: Referred to the House Committee on Education and Workforce.

bill.title: Recognizing the role of Mae Krier and her contributions as she celebrates her 100th birthday.

aiDescription.summary: This resolution thanks Mae Krier on her 100th birthday for serving as an original Rosie the Riveter at Boeing building B‑17 and B‑29 wings during World War II. It is an honorary, nonbinding House expression that specifically honors Krier and does not change law or policy.

impact.summary: If enacted, the House would adopt a nonbinding resolution thanking Mae Krier on her 100th birthday for her World War II service building Boeing B‑17 and B‑29 aircraft. It directly honors Mae Krier, her family, Boeing's Seattle workforce and the community of "Rosies" in the Congressional Record.
